dictations.preRound: Fell at home yesterday, tripped on a rug. Hip X-ray negative for fracture. Head CT negative. She uses an albuterol inhaler as needed. BMI 31. Not on anticoagulation. Pain 4 out of 10 in the left hip.
dictations.encounter: Bruising over the left hip, full range of motion. Walked 40 feet with a walker with PT. Acetaminophen 650 every 6 hours as needed. PT and OT to follow, likely discharge home with home health.

Physical Examination: Bruising over the left hip. Full range of motion of the left hip. Patient walked 40 feet with a walker with physical therapy.

Testing Results

Hip X-ray: negative for fracture.

Head CT: negative.

Assessment

Patient is a 78-year-old female with a history of asthma/reactive airway disease and obesity who was admitted after a fall at home yesterday, having tripped on a rug. Imaging workup including hip X-ray and head CT were obtained and are negative for fracture or intracranial injury. She has left hip pain rated 4 out of 10 with bruising over the left hip but maintains full range of motion. She ambulated 40 feet with a walker during physical therapy evaluation today. The clinical picture is consistent with a contusion of the left hip without fracture. She is not on anticoagulation. Pain is being managed with acetaminophen. Physical therapy and occupational therapy are engaged and anticipate discharge to home with home health services.

Plan

1. Continue acetaminophen 650 every 6 hours as needed for left hip pain.
2. Physical therapy and occupational therapy to continue; coordinate discharge planning with home health services.
3. Likely discharge home with home health support.
